headline: 30 Bangladeshi citizens returned home from Cambodia detention center
summary: The returnees were previously trapped in cyber-scamming centers and held in an immigration detention center after attempting to return home.
details: 30 Bangladeshi citizens arrived in Dhaka on Tuesday afternoon via a Thai Airways flight after being held in an immigration detention center in Cambodia.
The group had been detained by Cambodian immigration police at the Phnom Penh airport on September 3, while attempting to return to Bangladesh.
According to sources, the individuals were lured to Cambodia by brokers promising high-paying jobs, but were instead forced to work in cyber-scamming or online fraud centers.
The victims reported that those who attempted to escape from these scam centers faced torture.
Following a report by Jamuna Television on October 14, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment took initiatives to secure their release and repatriation.
Originally, 32 Bangladeshis were detained at the airport, but two were released earlier, leaving 30 in detention until their return today.
caption:
Lured by high salaries, 30 Bangladeshis were forced into cyber-scamming centers in Cambodia before being detained.

30 Bangladeshi citizens arrived in Dhaka on Tuesday afternoon via a Thai Airways flight after being held in an immigration detention center in Cambodia.

The group had been detained by Cambodian immigration police at the Phnom Penh airport on September 3, while attempting to return to Bangladesh.

According to sources, the individuals were lured to Cambodia by brokers promising high-paying jobs, but were instead forced to work in cyber-scamming or online fraud centers.

The victims reported that those who attempted to escape from these scam centers faced torture.

Following a report by Jamuna Television on October 14, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment took initiatives to secure their release and repatriation.

Originally, 32 Bangladeshis were detained at the airport, but two were released earlier, leaving 30 in detention until their return today.

Source: Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo

headline: President accepts Ishraque Hossain's resignation as state minister
summary: The resignation follows controversy over a video showing the minister holding a firearm during an anti-drug drive in Gendaria.
details: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has accepted the resignation of Ishraque Hossain, the state minister for Liberation War Affairs.
The Cabinet Division confirmed on Tuesday that the resignation took effect from Monday.
Ishraque, the son of former Dhaka City Corporation mayor Sadeque Hossain Khoka, announced his departure at a press conference at the National Press Club.
The decision came after controversy erupted over Facebook videos he posted of an anti-drug drive in Gendaria.
In the footage, Ishraque is seen participating in the drive while holding a firearm, raising questions about whether an elected representative should lead armed operations.
He stated that he resigned to prevent the government or the BNP from being embarrassed and to ensure the prime minister's work is not overshadowed.
The cabinet currently consists of 27 full ministers and 23 state ministers.
caption:
A state minister resigns after being filmed holding a gun during a police operation.

President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has accepted the resignation of Ishraque Hossain, the state minister for Liberation War Affairs.

The Cabinet Division confirmed on Tuesday that the resignation took effect from Monday.

Ishraque, the son of former Dhaka City Corporation mayor Sadeque Hossain Khoka, announced his departure at a press conference at the National Press Club.

The decision came after controversy erupted over Facebook videos he posted of an anti-drug drive in Gendaria.

In the footage, Ishraque is seen participating in the drive while holding a firearm, raising questions about whether an elected representative should lead armed operations.

He stated that he resigned to prevent the government or the BNP from being embarrassed and to ensure the prime minister's work is not overshadowed.

The cabinet currently consists of 27 full ministers and 23 state ministers.

#Bangladesh #Politics #Resignation #Dhaka #Government

Source: bdnews24.com, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo
